## A real crash fixed, per-type detection toggles, and 3x the flash headroom

The headline fix: **a genuine crash-on-commute bug is gone.** NimBLE was silently keeping its own permanent record of every distinct BLE address it had ever seen, completely separate from this project's own bounded 200-entry log -- because the scan runs indefinitely and never fires the scan-complete callback that would normally clear it. Sitting in one room, you'd never notice; driving past a steady stream of genuinely distinct devices (phones, headsets, cars, AirTags) is the worst possible case for exactly this leak, and it crashed the device after enough of them. One line fixes it: `scan->setMaxResults(0)`, NimBLE's own documented "callbacks only, don't retain" mode -- exactly what this project already does with every advertisement.

Also new: **per-type detection toggles.** A new TYPE FILTER row in Settings opens a screen listing all 14 detection types with an ON/OFF switch each. Too many AirTags flashing past on your commute? Turn AirTag off. A disabled type is dropped the moment it's classified -- never logged, counted, or alerted on -- not just hidden after the fact.

Under the hood, this release also nearly triples the flash headroom (89% used of a 1.25MB partition -> 37% of 3MB), by dropping the default two-slot OTA partition table for a single 3MB app partition. Nothing here has ever used OTA updates or the on-flash filesystem that table reserved space for, so it was pure waste. Every feature from here on has real room to work with instead of being a flash-budget negotiation.

### The actually-useful part
- **Fixed**: a real crash -- NimBLE's internal scan-results cache grew unbounded (one permanent allocation per distinct BLE address ever seen) since nothing ever capped or cleared it; heaviest exactly when driving past many genuinely distinct devices
- **Added**: per-type detection toggle -- a new TYPE FILTER row in Settings opens a screen to turn any of the 14 detection types on or off individually; a disabled type is never logged, counted, or alerted on
- **Fixed**: the aquarium background's rare shark used to get stuck oscillating around the center of the screen instead of ever crossing and despawning; it's also bigger, more visible, and startles fish it swims through now
- **Fixed**: closing Settings via the title-bar gear icon could also cycle the CLEAR screen's background, from the same tap
- **Added**: rare idle-screen flourishes on CLEAR (UFO flyby, stardust sparkles, a bird/bat critter, a glitchy one-liner) plus a matching fourth-wall wink from Squachy, all independent of which background style is active
- **Added**: LOCK BACKGROUND setting -- stops CLEAR's accidental tap-to-cycle gestures without touching the Settings screen's own BACKGROUND row
- **Changed**: nearly 3x the flash headroom (37% used of 3MB, was 89% of 1.25MB) by switching to a single-app partition table -- nothing here ever used OTA or on-flash storage
- **Changed**: ALERT's MORE INFO button is a taller two-line button in the corner instead of a wide one, so it no longer crowds the radar or the idle animations
- **Changed**: tapping GOT IT on an alert's explanation now returns straight to the main screen instead of back to the alert you just read about
- **Changed**: local/CI builds no longer build the frozen cyd35 environment by default
